title: The Governor of New York Kathy Hochul snubs the lunch date with Trump in protest against the threats of Pam Bondi
text:
Governor Kathy Hochul in New York agreed a lunch meeting with Donald Trump after the Ministry of Justice has launched lawsuits against her and her state about the status of the sanctuary.
Hochul was planned to sit with Trump on Thursday, but postponed it in the aftermath of the Bombshell rights, reported CBS News.
The move came only a few hours after Attorney General Pam Bondi had announced legal steps against New York and some of his leaders, including Hochul, for their positions in the midst of the migrant crisis.
Legal cases were also raised against New York AG Letitia James and Mark Schroeder, the current commissioner of the New York State Department of Motor Vehicles.
Bondi accused New York of prioritizing illegal immigrants over American citizens, and explains ‘it will stop today’.
At the height of the migrant crisis under the Biden administration, New York City received more than 10,000 migrants per month, and city leaders provided free hotel rooms and pre-paid credit cards.
The lawsuit of Bondi, submitted in the Northern district of New York, focuses in particular on the ‘Green Light Law’ of the state that grants illegal licenses for immigrants.
In response to the legal steps, Hochul described the move as ‘dramatic’ and promised to combat the performance of the Trump government.

In her press conference that announced the lawsuits, Bondi stated: “This is a new doj and we take steps to protect Americans.”
It comes after the Ministry of Justice has taken a similar action against Illinois and the city of Chicago last week.
“New York did not listen, so now you are the next one,” Bondi said, that the Ministry of Justice is also ready to go after other states that they believe they do not comply with federal law.
Bondi made her announcement with a group of federal law enforcement officials and an ‘Angel Mom’ Tammy Nobles who stood behind her.
Nobles shared the story of her daughter who was murdered by an immigrant and gang member who was illegal in the country. She could also be seen in a recent video of the White House.

The lawsuit argues that the law that goes back until 2019 is a “frontal attack on federal immigration laws, and the federal authorities that they manage.”
When asked by a reporter what the Ministry of Justice is looking for, Bondi said they should see with the leaders of New York, but they claimed that they must comply with federal law.
Hochul shot back late on Wednesday and called it a ‘worthless, publicity -driven court case’ and promised that the state would not go back.
